keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1206..1271 shape of 12,105 km2 (50 gazetteer cells) is Dordogne 23/38 cells, Lot-et-Garonne 20/22, Gironde 6/45, Lot 1/21: it spills over Agenais and the Gironde and holds only 60% of the Dordogne. The Brétigny list names 'Agenais, Périgord, Limousin, Quercy' as separate territories, so Lot-et-Garonne (Agenais) and the Gironde cells are not Périgord; neither the County of Périgord page (no infobox) nor the Périgord region page gives an area. Corrected to the Dordogne, 38 gazetteer cells (about 9,600 km2), the department of Périgueux.

correction.text: Périgord as the Dordogne under the Orléans, 1402-1439

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1402-1439 for years Cliopatria lacks (its row resumes in 1440): Louis I of Orléans is 'Count of Périgord 1400–1407' (infobox) and the Périgord region page says the county 'passed into the hands of the dukes of Orléans in the 15th century'. The pages give no holder for 1408-1439; the county is carried unchanged.

Unverified in outline: 18,176 km2, 76 cells = Dordogne 29/38, Corrèze 23/26, Lot-et-Garonne 7/22, Haute-Vienne 5/24, Lot 5/21, Cantal 2/23. The Corrèze and Haute-Vienne cells are Limousin, which the Brétigny list keeps apart from Périgord; the county-of-foix dossier cites the House of Albret page ('In 1470, they inherited the County of Périgord and the Viscounty of Limoges') for the two lordships being held together, which may be what the polygon draws. The Périgord pages opened give no area and no Limousin.

Unverified in outline: same polygon (18,223 km2). The Hundred Years' War ends at Castillon on 17 July 1453 and Bordeaux falls on 19 October (HYW page); the Périgord page calls the county 'one of the main battlegrounds' of the war.

Unverified in outline: same polygon to 1481. 'It passed into the hands of the dukes of Orléans in the 15th century, the d'Albrets in the 16th'; the page dates neither handover, so Cliopatria's end in 1481 is unchecked.

ledger.note: 1206: the County of Périgord, with its seat at Périgueux, is the earliest year of Cliopatria's shape. The pages date no founding; the page says the county was 'one of the main battlegrounds of Hundred Years' War'. The Périgord region page: Périgord and its neighbours were part of the 'English Angevin Empire during the 13th century'.

region.text: Périgord, listed among the lands Edward III obtained

ledger.note: October 1360: Périgord is ceded to Edward III by the Treaty of Brétigny. 'By the terms of this treaty, Edward III obtained Guyenne, Gascony, Poitou, Saintonge and Aunis, Agenais, Périgord,' ... 'drafted on 8 May 1360 and ratified on 24 October 1360'. The Cliopatria row has no shape 1363-1384.

region.text: Périgord, within the revolt of Aquitaine

ledger.note: 1369: war resumes over the Brétigny lands. 'In 1369, on the pretext that Edward III had failed to observe the terms of the treaty,' the French king declared war again (Brétigny page); 'before the end of 1369 all of Aquitaine was in full revolt' (this page). The pages do not name Périgord in the fighting.

1378: the French have retaken most of the ceded lands. 'By 1378, under King Charles V the Wise' (the page, under du Guesclin); 'by the time Charles V died in 1380, the English held only Calais and a few other ports.' Périgord is not named on the page, so the year is the page's and the land my reading.

1378: Périgord returns to the French side with the reconquest of the ceded lands (see the contest above); the duchy-of-aquitaine dossier (a cross-reference, not a page opened here) has the English loss of the Brétigny lands in 1377.

region.text: the county of Périgord, absorbed into the crown

ledger.note: 1398: the county is absorbed into the Kingdom of France: 'Périgord was eventually absorbed into the Kingdom of France in 1398.' The page gives no cause.

region.text: the county of Périgord, now held by Louis of Orléans

ledger.note: 1400: the crown's prince Louis of Orléans becomes Count of Périgord ('Périgord (1400–1407)', infobox 'Count of Périgord | 1400–1407').
1400: the House of Orléans takes the county ('the dukes of Orléans in the 15th century', Périgord region page); same state, same colour.

region.text: the county of Périgord (with Limousin cells) at the end of Cliopatria's row

ledger.note: 1481: Cliopatria's last year. The pages opened give the handover only as 'the d'Albrets in the 16th' century; the county-of-foix dossier has Périgord and the Viscounty of Limoges joining the Albret-Foix composite in 1484.

wars.name: Hundred Years' War in Périgord
wars.outcome: Périgord was ceded to England in 1360, the war resumed in 1369, the French retook most ceded lands by 1378, and the war ended at Castillon on 17 July 1453.
wars.note: 'one of the main battlegrounds of Hundred Years' War between the French and English in the 14th and 15th centuries' (this page); the dates of 1369, 1378 and 1453 are the HYW page's.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey on the pages opened; the Brétigny cession of 1360 lists regions, not lines. The extent is the Dordogne by the gazetteer, an approximation of Périgord.

notes:
Cliopatria reading by gazetteer cells: 1206-1271 and 1272-1401 are blocks of 50 and 35 cells that hold only 22-23 of the Dordogne's 38 cells and spill over Lot-et-Garonne (Agenais) and the Gironde, so all early shapes are marked adjust to the Dordogne; 1440-1481 (76 cells) adds Corrèze and Haute-Vienne (Limousin) and is kept unverified. The row has no shape 1363-1384 and 1402-1439; both gaps are filled by new keyframes from pages (1378 reconquest, Louis of Orléans 1400-1407 and the Orléans in the 15th century).
Thin pages: the County of Périgord and Périgord pages give no counts, no founding, no area and few dates; the failed pages were https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counts_of_P%C3%A9rigord, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archambaud_V,_Count_of_P%C3%A9rigord and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talleyrand-P%C3%A9rigord (url_not_found). The 1398 absorption and the 1400 grant to Louis of Orléans are page-dated but their cause and the holders of 1408-1481 are not; a gap-filler should open the French 'Comté de Périgord' page. The 1481 end and the successor (Albret-Foix) rest on Cliopatria and the county-of-foix dossier.
Cross-check: the kingdom-of-france dossier has Louis VIII taking Périgord in 1224 and the duchy-of-aquitaine dossier has the 1259 and 1360 changes; this dossier draws the county itself as continuous, with English or French overlords not tinted. The Dordogne adjustment removes the Lot-et-Garonne cells from the county in 1206-1401; they belong to Agenais (Aquitaine and Toulouse shapes).
